application_overview.name: Playwright TodoMVC & DemoQA Select Menu Exploration Dataset
application_overview.purpose: The evidence documents two distinct web domains explored during automated scanning: 1) A React-based Todo application hosted at demo.playwright.dev providing task input capabilities, and 2) A Select Menu component demonstration page on demoqa.com providing dropdown and selection widgets.
observed_functionality: Task creation text input with placeholder 'What needs to be done?' on React TodoMVC (demo.playwright.dev/todomvc/#/).
External resource hyperlinks to TodoMVC project and author profiles on React TodoMVC.
Single-selection HTML native dropdown (#oldSelectMenu) containing color choices on DemoQA.
Multi-selection HTML select list (#cars) containing car brand options on DemoQA.
Custom React-select text input controls (#react-select-2-input, #react-select-3-input, #react-select-4-input) on DemoQA.
Navigation link list for widgets (Accordian, Auto Complete, Date Picker, Slider, Progress Bar, Tabs, Tool Tips, Menu, Select Menu) on DemoQA.

pages.responsibility: Task management interface presenting an input field for capturing new todo items, alongside external reference links.
Widget demonstration page exposing native and custom React dropdown selection components.
observed_elements: a navigation links (Accordian, Auto Complete, Date Picker, Slider, Progress Bar, Tabs, Tool Tips, Menu, Select Menu)

business_workflows.workflow_name: Single Select Option Change via Old Select Menu
business_workflows.description: User interacts with native select dropdown #oldSelectMenu to change the selected option from default 'Red' to another value such as 'Blue'.
steps: Inspect the current value of select#oldSelectMenu (initial default value: 'red').
Verify that select#oldSelectMenu updates its value to '1'.
evidence: interactive_exploration.json: interaction_results[0] selector #oldSelectMenu previous_value 'red' selected_value '1' status 'success'

business_workflows.description: User enters task description into the main todo input field and submits to add an item to the list.
steps: Focus on input[placeholder='What needs to be done?'].
Type task name and press Enter key.
Observe if a list item or new UI element appears.
evidence: website_exploration.json: input with placeholder 'What needs to be done?'
ui_discovery_report.json: inputs[0] with placeholder 'What needs to be done?'

potential_test_scenarios.scenario_name: Verify single selection update in Old Select Menu
test_steps: Locate dropdown select element with id 'oldSelectMenu'.
Verify initial value is 'red'.
Select option with visible text 'Blue' and value '1'.
Read selected option value.
expected_results: The element value changes from 'red' to '1' and selected text displays 'Blue'.
evidence: interactive_exploration.json: interaction_results[0] selector #oldSelectMenu

potential_test_scenarios.scenario_name: Verify option bounds and total count in Old Select Menu
test_steps: Locate select element with id 'oldSelectMenu'.
Enumerate all child option elements.
Select the first option ('Red', value 'red').
Select the last option ('Aqua', value '10').
expected_results: The dropdown contains exactly 11 options, and boundary options 'Red' (first) and 'Aqua' (last) can be selected without error.
evidence: interactive_exploration.json: discovered_dropdowns[0] options array of length 11

potential_test_scenarios.scenario_name: Verify multi-select cars dropdown initial state and selection capability
test_steps: Locate select element with id 'cars'.
Verify type attribute is 'select-multiple'.
Verify initial selected value is empty.
Select option 'Volvo' (value 'volvo') and option 'Audi' (value 'audi').
expected_results: Multiple items ('volvo', 'audi') can be selected simultaneously without unchecking prior selections.
evidence: interactive_exploration.json: discovered_dropdowns[1] id 'cars' type 'select-multiple'

potential_test_scenarios.scenario_name: Validate initial rendering and attributes of TodoMVC input field
test_steps: Inspect the main input field.
Verify placeholder text equals 'What needs to be done?'.
Verify element is enabled (disabled equals false) and editable (readonly equals false).
Verify value_present is false on initial page load.
expected_results: Input field is displayed, enabled, empty, and displays the placeholder 'What needs to be done?'.
evidence: ui_discovery_report.json: inputs[0] with placeholder 'What needs to be done?', disabled: false, readonly: false, value_present: false

potential_test_scenarios.scenario_name: Attempt empty submission on TodoMVC input field
test_steps: Locate input[placeholder='What needs to be done?'].
Ensure input is empty.
Send Enter keystroke without typing any characters.
Check whether empty todo item is prevented from creation.
expected_results: No empty todo item is added to the application state or interface.
evidence: ui_discovery_report.json: inputs[0] placeholder 'What needs to be done?'

potential_test_scenarios.scenario_name: Boundary string length input in TodoMVC input field
test_steps: Locate input[placeholder='What needs to be done?'].
Enter a single character string ('A') and submit.
Enter a large character string (e.g., 255 characters or 1000 characters) and submit.
Verify input handling and layout stability.
expected_results: Application accepts valid single-character tasks and handles boundary long strings without breaking UI layout.
evidence: website_exploration.json: inputs[0]
ui_discovery_report.json: inputs[0]

assumptions: It is assumed that pressing Enter in the TodoMVC input field triggers task addition, although only the initial empty input state was captured in the evidence.
It is assumed that the multi-page exploration and ui_discovery_report target the TodoMVC application, whereas interactive_exploration was performed on DemoQA Select Menu.
It is assumed that the two domains (demo.playwright.dev and demoqa.com) were explored as separate target test subjects within the same exploration session.
missing_information: No recorded post-entry state or todo list elements exist in the TodoMVC evidence (no list items, checkboxes, filters, or delete buttons were discovered in the empty initial state).
No interaction records exist for DemoQA react-select input fields (#react-select-2-input, #react-select-3-input, #react-select-4-input).
No tables, search forms, or pagination controls were detected in any of the exploration logs.
user_confirmation_questions: Should test suite generation cover both demo.playwright.dev/todomvc and demoqa.com/select-menu, or should testing be isolated to a single target application?
Does the TodoMVC application require Enter key interaction or form submission to create items, and are completion checkboxes and filters expected once items exist?
What are the expected component behaviors and validation rules for the custom React select elements (#react-select-2-input, #react-select-3-input, #react-select-4-input) on DemoQA?
restrictions_applied: No production records or data were deleted or targeted for deletion.
No payment or financial transaction workflows were suggested or executed.
No unevidenced business logic or unseen pages were assumed; unobserved behaviors are marked with low confidence and flagged for user confirmation.
No modifications to live business data are proposed.
